meta.title: Czech Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 169 expressions · 50 everyday, 57 expressions, 15 idioms, 47 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 169 Czech set phrases, expressions, idioms and proverbs, in four subdecks: 50 everyday phrases, 57 expressions, 15 idioms and 47 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Czech → English (see the Czech, recall the meaning) and English → Czech (see an English meaning, recall the Czech) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the level decks, Czech A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of them, so they can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — the formulas a speaker uses as one piece (to je pravda, to znamená, děkuji ti, hodně štěstí …). The EXPRESSIONS are the fixed adverbials, verb phrases and compound prepositions and conjunctions Wiktionary carries as entries of more than one word (mít rád, jak dlouho, být rád, i když, mít na sobě …). The IDIOMS are the expressions with a sense Wiktionary marks as idiomatic, of any part of speech (být schopen, mít chuť, mít plné zuby, z ničeho nic, dělat z komára velblouda …). The PROVERBS are the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (chybovat je lidské, ranní ptáče dál doskáče, vrána k vráně sedá …). WHICH ONES: Wiktionary has 566 such Czech expressions that no level teaches, and this deck takes the 169 of them that occur in at least one of Tatoeba's Czech sentences with an English translation — an expression that begins with a verb being found with that verb in any form. That is a test of being in use, not an official list. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of those sentences contain them. Real example sentences come with 169 of the 169, three apiece for 50, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Meanings and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences and the count that chooses and orders the expressions: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

fields.Czech: to je pravda
fields.English:

fields.Czech: dobrý den

phrase

fields.Czech: jak se máte

phrase

phrase

phrase
